thread:
maria: heads-up — after the last merge master p95 for text-generation endpoints jumped ~20%. spotted via the synthetic perf canary run.

jason: ugh. which merge? commit hash?

maria: merge 0a7f3c2 — changes to fused-attn selection + batching heuristics. canary at 11:10 shows p95 150ms -> 182ms on short-decoding workload. tokens/s down ~12%.

ci-bot: perf/regression-checker reported: build 2025-03-18-411 — gpt-small-decode P95 +18% (baseline 160ms -> 189ms). link: https://ci.redwood/12345

eric: grabbing a profile from the canary VM now. attaching perf record.

eric: quick flamegraph: hotspots in decode path: attention_dispatch::select_kernel and attention_kernels::fused_attn_v2::execute

eric: perf top snippet:
```
 22.4%  runtime  [.] fused_attn_v2::execute
 11.8%  runtime  [.] memcpy
  9.5%  runtime  [.] kv_cache::apply_updates
```

sara: memcpy increase is weird. fused path was supposed to reduce copies by doing in-place ops.

jason: maybe the kernel selector is choosing an unfused fallback or v2's setup is doing extra copies. also batcher heuristics changed — could be shifting kernel mix.

maria: I reproduced locally comparing master vs revert-of-0a7f3c2:
```
master: p95 182ms
revert:  p95 146ms
```
Points to kernel_selector.rs and batcher_config.yaml changes.

oliver: running micro-bench to compare kernels (single step, seq_len=64, batch=8)

oliver: micro-bench results:
```
attn_unfused:  1.12 ms
fused_attn_v1: 0.95 ms
fused_attn_v2: 1.38 ms  <-- slower on short seqs
```

oliver: v2 is faster on long seqs (512) but our new heuristic picks v2 for many short requests because the seq_len threshold moved 256->128 and cost weights were adjusted.

jason: that would explain the p95 regression: the request mix shifted toward v2 for short-latency-sensitive traffic.

sara: can we change selector to prefer v1 for latency-sensitive routes or be p95-aware (not just mean cost)?

eric: additional detail: fused_attn_v2 includes a small memcpy in setup to align tensors to 128B. fine for batched throughput but adds per-request overhead on short requests.

maria: action items:
- revert batching heuristic tweak in batcher_config (quick)
- jason: open patch to adjust selector cost weights for short seqs
- eric/oliver: file issue to optimize v2 setup memcpy or add fast path for small buffers

jason: starting revert PR for batching heuristics now. CC @sara for rollout decision.

jason: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2109 — reverts seq_len threshold change and restores old cost weights. running CI.

ci-bot: runtime CI — build 2110 — perf-suite scheduled. waiting on bench results.

maria: while CI runs, oliver can you test local hotfix that forces selector to pick fused_attn_v1 when seq_len < 128?

oliver: done. local canary with hotfix: p95 -> 148ms. matches revert.

sara: this is a rollout blocker. pause the release until revert merged and canary validates.

deploy-bot: rollback blocked by PR #2110 status: pending. starting incremental canary hold.

jason: CI perf results (bench summary):
```
before (main): p95 182ms
after revert: p95 150ms (-17.6%)
```

ci-bot: perf/regression-checker: new build 2025-03-18-417 — PASS (regression resolved).

maria: OK. merge the revert once CI is green and coordinate immediate canary on dedicated pool with 10% traffic.

eric: follow-ups: instrument kernel_selector with counters (chosen kernel + seq_len histogram); add perf test exercising short-seq p95; re-evaluate v2 alignment strategy and remove unnecessary memcpy for small buffers.

sara: setting P0 and assigning tickets. I'll notify product and infra.

maria: thanks all — great catch. keep updates in this thread. if regression reappears after revert, ping me @maria.
